newsitem.title: INDIA: MERRILL LOWERS INDIAN INDUSTRIAL GROWTH FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: MERRILL LOWERS INDIAN INDUSTRIAL GROWTH FORECAST.

text.p: Investment bank Merrill Lynch said it revised its 1997/98 (April-March) forecast for Indian industrial growth to 8.0 percent from 10.0 percent.
"... Taking note of a sluggish first quarter, we are revising downward our FY1998 forecast from 10 percent to 8.0 percent," Merrill's India Economic Monthly of July 25 said.
But it said industrial growth is expected to pick up later this year on the back of falling interest rates.
Merrill expected good monsoon rains leading to healthy agricultural growth, but said a strong rupee was holding down Indian export growth.

"We believe that falling interest rates, rising stock market levels, improved agricultural production and tax incentives given in the budget will fuel higher industrial growth rates in the latter half of FY1998," the report said.

"However, most indicators such as credit offtakes, capital goods and machinery imports, and new equity issues do not indicate high industrial growth rates for the first and second quarter of FY1998," the report said.
"We believe this is in part due to the political uncertainty caused by a change in the government's leadership, which in turn is causing the current lack of consumer and corporate confidence."

"Barring any further political uncertainty, the positive factors listed above should push up consumption and investment demand, with much of the recovery showing through in the growth rates in 1998," it added.
